text: The strong Sapir-Whorf claim that language wholly determines thought -- so that thoughts inexpressible in one's language cannot be thought -- is today the well-supported consensus among researchers.
explanation: False. The strong (determinism) version is generally regarded as false; Whorf's flagship Hopi-time claim was largely debunked. Only the weak version -- that language influences but does not determine thought -- has received modest empirical support.
